botany.native_range: Sub-Saharan Africa: the savannas of the Sudanian and Sahelian zones, from Senegal to Sudan, and south into Mozambique, Madagascar and Australia for the genus as a whole.
botany.habitat: Seasonally dry savanna and open woodland, on ground that is waterlogged for part of the year and bone dry for the rest.
botany.climate: Hot, with a pronounced dry season. The most common African baobab grows where annual rainfall is roughly 100 to 600 mm and temperatures stay high year round.
distinguishing_characteristics: A single massive trunk that is wider than it is tall on mature specimens.
Smooth, grey-brown bark that is fire-resistant and re-grows after being scarred.
Large, palmate leaves clustered in tufts at the ends of the branches, shed during the dry season.
Flowers borne directly on the trunk and the oldest branches.
interesting_facts: Up to 80 percent of a mature baobab's mass can be water in its swollen trunk, which is how it survives the dry season.
The species is leafless for much of the year, so its silhouette is often mistaken for a dead tree.
Both the flowers and the fruit are pollinated by fruit bats, and the monkeys that eat the fruit disperse the seeds.
botany.attribution: Botanical summary compiled for Arboretum. Verify against the Kew Plants of the World Online record for Adansonia digitata before treating any specific figure as authoritative.

assets.note: The visual carrier is dark oak. Arboretum's standalone resource pack retextures dark oak into a baobab-inspired bark and foliage, so the species reads correctly with no mod installed. See docs/distribution.md.
